title: Microsoft Teams: meeting policy setting for numeric-only meeting passcodes
summary: The briefing matches the roadmap and Microsoft's documented meeting-policy setting. The admin path, PowerShell parameter, disabled default and effect on newly scheduled meetings are supported; licensing is correctly described using the general Teams requirement.

claims.where: front matter: roadmapModified

claims.where: What's changing: second paragraph
claims.claim: The roadmap describes a setting tenant admins can enable for meetings organised by selected users or groups.
claims.quote: Tenant admins can enable a meeting policy setting that generates 8 digit numeric-only passcodes for meetings organized by selected users/groups.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; controls[0].ui
claims.claim: Allow numeric-only meeting passcodes makes meetings use 8-digit numeric-only passcodes.
claims.quote: Allow numeric-only meeting passcodes | Off | Controls whether meetings use 8-digit numeric-only passcodes.

claims.where: What's changing: first paragraph; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The system default is an 8-character alphanumeric passcode.
claims.quote: Default: Alphanumeric passcodes with 8 characters (system default).

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; controls[0].note; rationales
claims.claim: The numeric-only setting is off by default and requires an administrator to enable it, supporting admin-opt-in.
claims.quote: Changes apply only to meetings scheduled after the setting is enabled. Existing meetings are not affected. This setting is disabled by default.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; Governance controls; controls[0].scope
claims.claim: This setting operates through meeting policies for the users to whom each policy applies, rather than as one tenant-wide switch.
claims.quote: When enabled, meetings scheduled by users to whom this policy applies will use 8‑digit numeric‑only passcodes.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; controls[0].note; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Enabling the setting applies only to meetings scheduled afterwards.
claims.quote: Changes apply only to meetings scheduled after the setting is enabled.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; controls[0].note
claims.claim: Existing meetings are not affected by the setting.
claims.quote: Existing meetings are not affected.

claims.where: What's changing: second paragraph; Governance controls
claims.claim: The roadmap says enabling the setting displays a warning.
claims.quote: Because numeric-only passcodes increase the risk of unauthorized access, enabling the setting displays a warning and requires explicit confirmation.

claims.where: What's changing: second paragraph; Governance controls
claims.claim: The roadmap says enabling the setting requires explicit confirmation.
claims.quote: enabling the setting displays a warning and requires explicit confirmation.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Numeric-only passcodes have lower complexity and increase the risk of unauthorised meeting access.
claims.quote: Numeric-only passcodes have lower complexity and increase the risk of unauthorized access to meetings.

claims.where: What's changing: second paragraph; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: The PowerShell reference says numeric-only passcodes do not align with Microsoft's recommended meeting security best practices.
claims.quote: Numeric‑only passcodes increase the risk of unauthorized access compared to the default setting and do not align with Microsoft’s recommended meeting security best practices.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The Teams admin center path is Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Edit > Meeting join & lobby > Allow numeric-only meeting passcodes.
claims.quote: Meeting join & lobby; Navigation: Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies; Allow numeric-only meeting passcodes. The cited meeting-policies-overview page adds: Choose the policy by clicking to the left of the policy name, and then select Edit.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -PasscodeComplexity NumericOnly configures numeric-only passcodes in MicrosoftTeams PowerShell.
claims.quote: Module: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell module; Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy; -Identity: Specify the name of the policy being created. NumericOnly: 8‑digit numeric‑only passcodes with lower complexity for meetings scheduled by users to whom this policy applies.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Setting -PasscodeComplexity Default restores the system-default alphanumeric format for newly scheduled meetings.
claims.quote: Controls whether meeting passcodes use the system‑default complexity or a reduced complexity using numeric‑only digits. Default: Alphanumeric passcodes with 8 characters (system default).

claims.where: Scope: first paragraph; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Users receive the global meeting policy unless a custom policy is created and assigned.
claims.quote: Users get the global policy unless you create and assign a custom policy.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Scope
claims.claim: A user can be assigned only one meeting policy at a time.
claims.quote: A user can be assigned only one meeting policy and one events policy at a time.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: Before rollout and At rollout
claims.claim: Administrators can create and assign a custom meeting policy to give chosen users different settings from the global policy.
claims.quote: You can edit the settings in the global policy or create and assign one or more custom policies.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The setting uses the product's Teams licence requirement, supporting included; organisational users need a Teams licence except to join meetings anonymously.
claims.quote: You manage access to Teams at the user level by assigning or removing a Microsoft Teams product license. Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No licence requirement specific to numeric-only meeting passcodes is published at the time of writing in November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams "numeric-only" "license" "passcodes". Read Manage Teams licenses, the settings and policies reference, Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy, and the meetings overview; these give the general Teams requirement but no licence specific to this setting.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: first paragraph
claims.claim: The roadmap record names no licence requirement.
claims.quote: Tenant admins can enable a meeting policy setting that generates 8 digit numeric-only passcodes for meetings organized by selected users/groups.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: second paragraph; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The referenced pages publish no price for the numeric-only setting.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams "numeric-only" passcodes price credit rate limit; site:learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams "numeric-only" "price". Opened the settings reference, Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy, Manage Teams licenses and the meetings overview; no setting-specific price appears.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: second paragraph
claims.claim: The referenced pages publish no credit rate for the numeric-only setting.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: second paragraph

claims.quote: Searched: Teams "numeric-only" passcodes price credit rate limit. Read the settings reference, Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy, Manage Teams licenses and the meetings overview; none gives a consumption or spending limit for the setting.

claims.where: Governance controls: final paragraph
claims.claim: The pages used for this briefing do not state the role needed to edit meeting policies.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams numeric-only meeting passcodes licensing price PasscodeComplexity default role TeamsAdminAction; role/administrator in the settings and PowerShell references. Read meeting-policies-overview: it gives editing steps without a required role.

claims.where: Open questions: delegate bullet
claims.claim: For an authorised delegate sending a meeting invitation for someone else, the meeting policy applies to the person who granted permission.
claims.quote: When a delegate authorized to send meeting invitations for someone else sends a meeting, the meeting policy applies to the person who granted the delegate permission.

claims.where: Open questions: audit bullet
claims.claim: Microsoft documents TeamsAdminAction for Teams administrators updating, adding or deleting Teams settings or configurations through administrative tools.
claims.quote: Teams Admin Action | TeamsAdminAction | Logged when a Teams admin performs actions like updating, adding, or deleting Teams related settings or configurations using admin tools like PowerShell, Admin Center, API, etc.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: This setting changes passcode generation rather than adding an agent or autonomous action.
claims.quote: Controls whether meeting passcodes use the system‑default complexity or a reduced complexity using numeric‑only digits.
